state.acceptanceRules: Evaluate aggregate boundary design, not whether a command route or test is complete. One owner per independently changing identity/lifecycle unless a named invariant requires atomic shared state. Keep cross-owner decisions in handlers using exact proofs; never rely on projections as authority. Avoid unbounded unrelated history or invented lifetime caps. A split is sound only when its coordinator/reservations preserve the invariant and have durable retry/recovery.

rows.name: AccessGrant
rows.invariant: One stable grant identity has one immutable set of scope/principal/effective terms and, once revoked, can never be reissued.
rows.splitTest: Splitting terms from revocation could permit reissue or activation with mismatched membership episode. No other grants need the same revision.
rows.identity: Tenant+grantId; caller supplies stable grant identity. Issue compares terms/episode; Revoke exact retry conflicts. Portia expected stream position handles append OCC.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Scalar current terms, episode, revoked. At most two business facts per grant; lifecycle domain replay is bounded independently of number of grants.
rows.contention: Only one grant lifecycle; no parent roster.
rows.events: Issued and revoked are business authority facts; validation failures produce no events. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.
rows.crossOwner: Handler supplies validated proposal/current membershipEpisodeId value; aggregate reads no other owner. Separate member eligibility is admission and later authority checks.
rows.decisionStatus: retained boundary; implementation findings remain

rows.name: FirmProfessionalDutyCatalog
rows.invariant: One active signed designation per user+duty+tenant; refresh/revoke must supersede exact assertion with increasing authority revision and stable subject.
rows.splitTest: Per-duty predecessor lineage and tuple uniqueness matter; unrelated tenants/users do not require one global revision. Global assertion identity may need separate reservation.
rows.identity: Global fixed CatalogId; requestID+intent+actor retry map; expected global Sequence and exact predecessor enforce conflicts/OCC.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Dictionaries of every designation, continuity starts, latest signed assertions; seenAssertionIDs and request responses grow every change. Domain replay grows all firm duty lifetimes.
rows.contention: Any unrelated designation refresh invalidates global sequence.
rows.events: Recorded/revoked designation business facts retain full view and signed proof; request/expectedSequence are technical envelope duplicates, rule16 pending. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.
rows.crossOwner: Verified assertion and staff view passed as values after handler admission; no aggregate reads another.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: FirmStaffDirectory
rows.invariant: Canonical user maps to exactly one immutable staff identity/practice; each staff status changes at its revision.
rows.splitTest: User uniqueness needs authoritative slot; independent employee activity does not need shared global revision.
rows.identity: Fixed global DirectoryId; request intent+actor replay map; expected global Sequence and append OCC.
rows.stateAndGrowth: All staff including inactive plus all request responses;1000 lifetime registrations and unbounded status events.
rows.contention: Status change for any staff invalidates everybody else.
rows.events: Staff registration/status are business facts packaged as operation+full view; same-status new request still increments revision. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.
rows.crossOwner: Handler performs canonical platform-user admission, aggregate takes only values.

rows.name: IndependenceLedger
rows.invariant: Permanent tenant+person practice exclusivity and acceptance only against exact client service history, reviewed draft, personal acknowledgement and ratified-rule proofs.
rows.splitTest: Separating unchecked assignments or acceptance from source history would break real independence rules. Independent draft editing/history/evaluation lifecycles need no all-tenant atomicity once authoritative admission coordination exists.
rows.identity: Tenant singleton; global Sequence and per-request normalized intent+actor response maps. Exact retries generally recognized before sequence gates; all append OCC inherited.
rows.stateAndGrowth: All services/evaluations, engagements/every revision, tentative/current/permanent actual assignments, acknowledgements, acceptances/every revision, source/assignment/directory reevaluations and partner evaluations; repeated complete snapshots. Caps100/1000 and48KiB payload rejection constrain accepted business, not natural lifetime.
rows.contention: All tenant edits, judgments, staff and source changes conflict. Some coupling preserves source completeness; much unrelated lifecycle contention remains.
rows.events: Service, acceptance, personal management/partner decisions can be valid business facts. Reevaluation establishes denial/review obligation and must not be called invalid merely because named receipt; repeated full snapshots and technical Intent amplify storage. One command legitimately emits cause+several accepted review facts. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.
rows.crossOwner: All external staff/rules/boundary/authority passed as frozen or verified values. No partial reads another aggregate directly. Separate source epoch and person-practice invariant need preserve during split.

rows.splitTest: Global version allocation/current activation requires atomic sequence; historical documents do not need retained command-state list.

rows.stateAndGrowth: Full immutable rule versions+responses;100 version lifetime cap. Replay must load every source rule.
rows.contention: Single global rule sequence justified for one active catalog, not arbitrary unrelated lifecycles.

Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.

rows.name: IndependenceRuleRatificationCatalog
rows.invariant: Only valid professional proof can ratify an exact immutable rule digest, and active ratified rule version advances monotonically.

Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. rows.name: Member
rows.invariant: One tenant-user membership has one affiliation/expiry episode; deprovision closes authority and a fresh episode cannot start until authority cleanup completes.
rows.splitTest: Affiliation, lifecycle and current episode must change together. Cleanup completion is an authority-release gate; membership roster/grants remain external.
rows.identity: UUIDv5 tenant+user. New episode minted on accepted re-registration. Current flags make some retries no-ops but no operation+episode identity fences old commands. Append OCC serializes member writes.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Current lifecycle fields and last deprovision evidence, no child roster. Every suspend/reinstate/deprovision/register cycle adds lifetime replay; no bound or recovery sizing evidence supplied.
rows.contention: Per-person lifecycle contention is justified; manager coordinator cross-writes add protocol risk.
rows.events: Registered/suspended/reinstated/deprovisioned are facts. CleanupCompleted should be modeled as accepted authority-release fact (permits new episode), with technical cleanup progress outside domain. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.

rows.stateAndGrowth: Current name/defined/deleted. Rename history unbounded across role lifetime; no collection.

rows.name: RolePermission

rows.splitTest: Relationship can be assigned/removed without serializing unrelated permissions; a roster in Role is unnecessary.
rows.identity: UUIDv5 tenant+role+normalized permission. Current bool handles immediate Assign retry; lacks assignment/request identity for replay after removal; repeated Remove notFound.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Scalar assigned; repeated grant/remove cycles grow lifetime replay without bound.
rows.contention: Per tuple only; parent Role revision not shared.
rows.events: Assigned/removed authority facts; no receipt events. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. rows.name: SeparationOfDutiesWaiver
rows.invariant: Exact record/version/action/beneficiary exception can be approved once only by a different administrator who is neither requester nor beneficiary, during its validity window.
rows.splitTest: Request scope/actors and approval must remain one authority. Another waiver has independent lifecycle.
rows.identity: Create waiverId=context.RequestId. Record normalized terms compare; approval exact approver retry no-op and changed approver conflict. Expected-position OCC.
rows.stateAndGrowth: One request, one approval; max two facts naturally by lifecycle, not invented cap.
rows.contention: Per waiver only.
rows.events: Requested and independently approved exception are meaningful facts; no rejection events. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.
rows.crossOwner: Member eligibility is handler admission through membership reader. Aggregate receives values; it owns separation among its own recorded actors, not external role truth.
rows.decisionStatus: retained boundary; implementation findings remain

rows.name: Team

rows.splitTest: Membership and role assignments need independent lifecycles, which current design already supplies; team itself owns only existence/deletion.
rows.identity: Caller stable teamId in tenant stream; Define unconditional existing no-op hides changed intent. Expected-position OCC.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Two flags; at most definition+deletion naturally; no membership roster retained.
rows.contention: Per-team only.
rows.events: Defined/deleted facts; no negative receipt. rows.name: TeamMember
rows.invariant: One tenant/team/member relationship is active only for one current membership episode.
rows.splitTest: Membership episode and active flag must be together; team-wide roster does not need an atomic revision. Tenant-manager invariant requires separate authoritative removal coordination.

rows.splitTest: Each role assignment lifecycle independent; Team need not own collection. Critical built-in role removal policy remains external command admission.
rows.identity: UUIDv5 tenant/team/role; immediate Assign retry no-op, older replay after Remove reassigns; repeated Remove notFound; append OCC.

rows.name: TenantManagerGuard
rows.invariant: Removal from effective administrator set must leave another active tenant administrator.
rows.splitTest: Without a shared authoritative decision/hold two removals could each rely on the other. The coordination boundary is justified; guard-to-member transition protocol is incomplete.
rows.identity: Tenant singleton, observed Sequence value, reasons per member, append OCC. Reasons suppress immediate duplicate withdrawal but no operation/generation token binds source write or restoration.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Withdrawn members with reason sets, not full team roster. Restorations remove active state; lifetime decisions unbounded across all membership changes.
rows.contention: Global administrator authority contention justified. It also records nonadmin suspension withdrawals, which can accumulate unrelated members until restored.
rows.events: Withdrawn/restored reflect authority holds; process reservations should remain technical coordinator state unless explicit business authority effect is intended. Payloads often repeat tenant/subject/actor/timestamps already partly present in Portia metadata; rule16 wording is truncated, so no blanket rule16 violation is assigned. Discriminator attributes inspected; no rename is proposed while rule18 clarification is pending.
rows.crossOwner: Guard receives boolean value proof; service hydrates actual member/assignment and uses directory only to enumerate candidates, rechecks source. Not projection-substitution.
rows.decisionStatus: retained boundary; implementation findings remain

rows.name: AccessPopulation
rows.invariant: An accepted population is an immutable, internally valid snapshot; each accepted principal classification has a contiguous decision count and valid identity shape.
rows.splitTest: Separating mutable draft facts from acceptance without a fence permits accepting a different set than the validated snapshot. Principal classification decisions can be separate from the immutable population using exact accepted-population and principal proofs; nothing requires classifications of unrelated principals to serialize.
rows.identity: tenant/access-populations/populationId; Open handler uses stable request identity. Open compares initial creation terms. Record uses population Revision; Classify uses principal history count but both append to the same physical stream. Mutation retry receipts are absent for Record/Classify.

stateAndGrowth.retained: Whole current principal/entitlement/group/assignment graph plus every classification decision of every principal.
stateAndGrowth.lifetimeReplay: Draft replacements, acceptance and repeated classifications accumulate forever in one population stream; MaximumFacts bounds current graph, not replacements or classification history.

rows.contention: All principal classifications and draft edits use one physical revision despite per-principal logical counts.
rows.events: Opened/facts-recorded/accepted/classified are substantive snapshot and classification decisions. Scope/actor/time also occur in payload; rule16 unresolved. No refusal event on validation failures.
rows.crossOwner: Handler checks Person/ServiceIdentity existence and application visibility at admission; aggregate receives IDs and immutable facts, no live aggregate argument.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: AccessReviewCampaign
rows.invariant: Completion is admitted only after every frozen review item is decided and each required remediation is verified or covered by a live exception; reviewer and remediation owner stay distinct per item.
rows.splitTest: A naive item split breaks the atomic completion gate: a new or changed decision can invalidate remediation while completion uses an old summary. Keep a campaign completion coordinator with sealed item generations/completion proofs, while independent review/remediation item lifecycles move to their own streams.
rows.identity: tenant/access-review-campaigns/context.RequestId; itemId derives from campaign+population+subject+entitlement. Revision shared across all commands. Reassignment has exact-intent replay; Decide only matches decisionId and returns previous decisions regardless of changed intent.

stateAndGrowth.retained: All frozen items and ordering, per-item complete decision/change/reassignment histories, verification/exception and campaign-wide retry map.
stateAndGrowth.lifetimeReplay: Frozen item count may be large; repeated decisions/provider changes/reassignments grow command state and replay without bound before completion.

rows.contention: An unrelated item decision advances Revision and invalidates every in-flight remediation/reassignment/complete command.
rows.events: Review decisions, changes, verification and completion are owner facts. Bulk command correctly establishes several item decisions in one event. Frozen item list is copied into launch event; no event size guard. Retry acknowledgements are return values, not separate native events.
rows.crossOwner: Decide receives live SeparationOfDutiesWaiver and calls Allows. Launch handler supplies frozen snapshots/value items from other owners, which is admission and does not require live aggregate reads inside campaign.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: AccessReviewSystemLedger
rows.invariant: Each expectation can be independently approved by someone other than its proposer unless exactly waived; an approved successor changes the effective expectation line. Exceptions require an approved expectation and future expiry.
rows.splitTest: Unrelated expectations and missing-population exceptions have no joint atomic rule. Split expectation lineage by business rule identity; coordinate successor admission only with its own predecessor and keep system coverage as a projection. Exceptions are their own decisions with their own IDs.
rows.identity: tenant/access-review-systems/systemInstanceId; all IDs are child identities. Every mutation checks one ledger Revision. Propose only compares proposer for reused expectationId; exceptions return reused IDs without intent comparison.

stateAndGrowth.retained: All expectation versions, proposer map, every rule exception and every missing-population exception.
stateAndGrowth.lifetimeReplay: Every expectation, supersession and expiring exception remains retained for system lifetime; no lifetime bound.

rows.contention: One exception changes shared revision of all other unrelated approvals.
rows.events: Approval and exception facts are substantive owner decisions. Event payload contains nested full view snapshots and scope/actor; rule16 unresolved. Rejection emits no technical event.
rows.crossOwner: Approve takes live SeparationOfDutiesWaiver, invokes Allows. Other system/existence facts are handler admission values.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: AdvisorHandoff
rows.invariant: Feedback admission must occur while this handoff is ready and unrevoked/closed, against an exactly selected source version. Feedback corrections/responses preserve original contribution; selection change makes feedback historical.
rows.splitTest: Naively splitting feedback loses atomic admission-versus-revocation gate. Retain compact handoff admission authority; individual feedback and its correction/response lifecycle can live separately under exact admission proof. No write rule spans two feedback items.
rows.identity: Tenant / advisor-handoffs / handoffId; feedbackId/correctionId supplied; create compares current selection not original after selection changes; responses have no command/response identity and always append; end/readiness/selection exact retries fail state/revision. Pinned Portia uses full physical stream replay and expected physical position; no durable request dedup is supplied.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Current selection max100, but all feedback with all correction/response lists retained forever and read from aggregate. Every feedback operation extends lifetime replay; no lifecycle cap.
rows.contention: All unrelated feedback threads and access/selection/revocation operations share handoff physical revision.
rows.events: Creation/readiness/access end and contributed feedback are business facts. Delta feedback events are not receipts; response facts lack stable intent identity. Truncated rules16/18/21 await clarification; explicit business actor/signer snapshots were not automatically treated as equivalent to metadata.Actor.
rows.crossOwner: Exact source-reference values only; handlers establish actor/resource authority. No public method takes a live aggregate.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: ApplicationImportLedger
rows.invariant: One source has at most one acceptance in progress; source record identities cannot be rebound, and source acceptance becomes visible only when every sealed target effect is durable at its exact expected revision.
rows.splitTest: Source-wide epoch/admission gate is real, but all execution plans and per-record claims need not share it forever. Narrow coordinator, recoverable ordered reservations and complete seal must preserve original atomic acceptance; per-target commands alone lose it.
rows.identity: Source identity length-encodes source key/namespace with tenant. Batch/submission ids stable. Acceptance/correlation check prior intent, but business and technical histories are retained as dedup maps.
rows.stateAndGrowth: All cancellations, correlations, committed revisions, frozen plan rows, failures and accepted source bindings across every batch retained.200 effects bounds one batch, not lifetime.
rows.contention: Every batch, correlation and retirement proposal for same source shares revision. Per-record source binding is independent except complete source epoch/acceptance seal.
rows.events: Frozen rows/seal/pending receipts are process evidence and technical bindings currently DomainEvents. Source accepted/canceled and immutable source claims may be domain facts; do not delete technical durability before process recovery is provided.
rows.crossOwner: Methods receive live ImportBatch and DeclaredApplication dictionaries for admission, commit verification and retirement. Multi-target application effects follow plan order rather than canonical target hold order. A seal-triggered execution reactor exists, but receiver conflict/recovery remains material.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: DeclaredApplication
rows.invariant: An application has immutable creation intent, versioned metadata and retirement eligibility; retirement requires an approved successor for the exact source revision. Import reservation must prevent conflicting local changes until durable settlement.
rows.splitTest: Metadata/retirement and a narrow admission generation remain with application. Relationship identities have separate lifecycles. Splitting them requires source retirement/admission holds and unique active relationship tuple claims; no projected roster can enforce successor or active-source rule.
rows.identity: Per-application identity. Initial declaration fields retained for changed-intent check. Revisions/retirement lack selected RequestId dedup. Relationships mix tuple-derived and caller ids and retry checks omit portions of intent.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Current metadata bounded but all relationship histories and all pending import effects retained; physical replay grows across every relationship and import interaction.
rows.contention: Application metadata, relationship approvals/removals and independent import sources share physical revision, although logical relationship revisions mask part of contention.
rows.events: ApplicationDeclared/Retired are owner facts. ImportEffectPending is technical binding; importing commitment from another stream changes application business state without an owner-native committed fact in the application stream.
rows.crossOwner: ResolveImportVisibility calls live ledger and mutates _created/_retired/_revision. Production ApplicationImportWriteGuard hydrates each source ledger and supplies committed event ids to constructor. Application state depends on external settlement proof at replay, not just own stream. RecordPendingImportEffect also calls ledger authorization.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: DeclaredSystemInstance
rows.invariant: One system instance has one immutable application parent and registered identity; metadata revisions and terminal retirement follow its own expected revision.
rows.splitTest: Separating independent instances is already safe. Immutable parent binding and retirement gate belong with this instance, rather than parent roster state.
rows.identity: Per instance minted/business id; declaration compares current fields, retirement rejects already-retired retry, revision commands have no selected logical request lookup.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Scalar current state is bounded; revisions still accumulate indefinitely in the physical stream. Repository hydration reads full history.
rows.contention: Per instance contention is coherent. Parent program/application listings belong in projections.
rows.events: Registration/revision/retirement business facts; legacy application-stream instance facts require explicit read compatibility ownership.
rows.crossOwner: Parent identity is a value. Registration/retirement admission checks should pass value proof if parent status matters.
rows.decisionStatus: retained boundary; implementation findings remain

rows.name: ImportBatch
rows.invariant: A stable source submission has exactly one immutable digest and bounded staged row set; the same submission identity cannot be rebound to changed rows.
rows.splitTest: Splitting rows without an immutable digest/seal would lose complete submission identity. Keep a finite staged capsule; chunk storage if transport requires, without making each immutable row an aggregate.
rows.identity: BatchIdFor derives tenant, length encoded source key/namespace and stable SubmissionId, distinguishing retry from new submission. Same digest retry no-ops; changed digest conflicts. Legacy Cancel accepts any canceled retry with expectedRevision<=Revision, ignoring changed reason/actor.

stateAndGrowth.current: Immutable row set and staging metadata.
stateAndGrowth.lifetimeReplay: Intrinsically finite stage/cancel lifecycle; row cap200/48KiB are submission/transport limits rather than a lifetime fact cap. Their business/transport derivation still needs justification.

rows.contention: Per submission, unrelated batches independent. Legacy cancellation also exists on source ledger, so classify migration ownership explicitly.
rows.events: Staged immutable input is a fact; legacy cancellation emitters must not establish competing cancellation authority.
rows.crossOwner: Source acceptance lives separately. ImportBatch should supply an immutable digest/row proof at admission, not be passed as a live aggregate into another stream.
rows.decisionStatus: retained boundary; implementation findings remain

rows.name: SystemInstanceAccessReviewScope
rows.invariant: Scope decisions for one instance advance a monotonic effective date and expected decision sequence with independent approver or exact-scope waiver.
rows.splitTest: Current decision and last effective date must remain ordered. Historical decisions are read history, not independent mutable owners. Moving the list to projection must retain the current/sequence gate.
rows.identity: Stream uses instance id. DecisionId lookup returns prior success without comparing changed decision, reason, actor, effective dates or instance version.
rows.stateAndGrowth: All historical decisions retained in _decisions and EffectiveAt scans history; full replay and list grow for instance lifetime.
rows.contention: Per-instance decisions are related; unrelated historical display and live instance/waiver behavior need not remain in this owner.
rows.events: Accepted scope decision is a business fact. Native decision identity must compare complete immutable intent; audit attribution should use metadata where equivalent.
rows.crossOwner: Decide accepts live DeclaredSystemInstance and live SeparationOfDutiesWaiver and calls their behavior; even value ScopedSystemInstance overload still calls waiver.Allows. Owner should receive verified exact-scope value proof and enforce its own ordering/independence.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: AuditPackage
rows.invariant: A delivery must use exact selected manifest and successful archive, passed/current validation or independent complete overrides, and approval for recipient; delivered version content cannot change.
rows.splitTest: Those authorization gates require a compact coordinator/one-use delivery authorization after split. Build attempts, deliveries to different recipients and prior immutable versions need not live as parent state.
rows.identity: Tenant / audit-packages / packageId; child IDs derived from manifest version and key/recipient; package expectedRevision; create retry includes generated timestamp and only works while currentVersion=1. Portia appends against the hydrated physical stream position; a logical revision does not create another physical boundary.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Every immutable version, selected source manifest, all builds/validations/overrides/disclosures/deliveries copied into each event. Caps of64 builds,64 validations,64 approvals,128 deliveries; unbounded versions can hit 512KiB full-state bound.
rows.contention: A progress update or another recipient delivery invalidates unrelated validation/approval/amendment revision.
rows.events: Build progress is technical workflow state; exact successful archive, validation decisions and delivery authorization are domain outcomes. Events serialize entire historical package. Event discriminator stability and detailed metadata policy await clarification of truncated rules 16/18; duplicate envelope fields were observed, not automatically removed. Global CORE-01 applies: serialization through statically DomainEvent measures {} rather than the derived payload in these guards; nominal byte bounds are ineffective, confirmed against pinned DLL by root probe.
rows.crossOwner: Handlers resolve/fence source values. Aggregate accepts content/output/findings values and never reads live other owners.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation

rows.name: AuditPopulation
rows.invariant: Freeze must bind exact definition, source inventories and complete per-category row reconciliation; frozen content is immutable and incomplete reconciliation stays sample-ineligible.
rows.splitTest: Keep current complete row/category/source reconciliation and authoritative freeze seal together. Immutable row/version content may use chunked capsules and history projections; independent export attempts need their own process/identity. No per-row projected counts may decide freeze.
rows.identity: Tenant / audit-populations / populationId (Define handler uses DefinitionId); definition/source/row/export identities checked; one shared expectedRevision; several mutators check revision before retry. Portia appends against the hydrated physical stream position; a logical revision does not create another physical boundary.
rows.stateAndGrowth: Current rows/sources plus every frozen copy, definition version, amendment and export live in each State. 64 versions and256 exports cap lifetime;512KiB complete-state bound blocks normal growth sooner for rich rows.
rows.contention: Classification of one row, new source collection, export and definition/version operations all share one revision.
rows.events: Row/classification/reconciliation/freeze are business facts; Generated only marks collection intent despite completed-sounding discriminator. Every event copies historical full state. Event discriminator stability and detailed metadata policy await clarification of truncated rules 16/18; duplicate envelope fields were observed, not automatically removed. Global CORE-01 applies: serialization through statically DomainEvent measures {} rather than the derived payload in these guards; nominal byte bounds are ineffective, confirmed against pinned DLL by root probe.
rows.crossOwner: Define accepts a TypeIIPeriodView value and checks immutable close snapshot; handlers hydrate authoritative period. No live aggregate reference.
rows.decisionStatus: retain current complete reconciliation/freeze gate; independent export lifecycle split is conditional

rows.name: AuditorRequest
rows.invariant: A response must be independently reviewed if required before exact delivery; request resolution requires at least one response and accepted external disposition for every admitted response.
rows.splitTest: Splitting all responses without registration/sealing loses the all-responses-accepted rule. Comment and sample selection lifecycles require no request-member atomic state; response coordinator can retain admission/count/closure proofs.
rows.identity: Tenant / auditor-requests / requestId; response/selection IDs supplied, comments minted random in aggregate with no command key; many handlers pass current aggregate.Revision automatically; creation compares generated timestamp. Portia appends against the hydrated physical stream position; a logical revision does not create another physical boundary.
rows.stateAndGrowth: All terms/history/comments/responses/all response versions/deliveries/dispositions/sample selections kept and copied each event; caps256 comments,64 responses,16 versions,64 selections,512 total history and48KiB state bound.
rows.contention: A comment makes an independent response review/delivery stale; all responses and samples contend.
rows.events: Comments, response decisions/delivery/disposition are business facts; rejects/changes_requested are accepted auditor/reviewer facts, not denied-command receipts. State events repeat all prior facts. Event discriminator stability and detailed metadata policy await clarification of truncated rules 16/18; duplicate envelope fields were observed, not automatically removed.
rows.crossOwner: Evidence/population/member checks occur in handlers; aggregate accepts values only. Open request admission must become explicit source-owner authorization if children split.
rows.decisionStatus: provisional scope recommendation; concrete protocol and final exact-head review required before implementation
